{{Quote|Ho'Din are not limited to their eyes and ears, princess. We never forget our friends.|[[Spero]]|<ref name="Shadows of the Empire (novel)">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>}}
'''Ho'Din''' were tall [[Alien/Legends|aliens]], renowned throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] for their botanical and healing abilities.

==Biology and culture==
<!-- The words in single square brackets are supposed to be like that. No need to change them. -->
[[File:Hodingg4.jpg|thumb|left|141px|A male Ho'Din]]
{{Quote|Almost all Ho'Din know how to work medical miracles using plants and herbs. They're a race of healers, your Excellency.|[[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Bertroff Hissa]] to [[Trioculus]]|<ref name="The Lost City of the Jedi">''[[The Lost City of the Jedi]]''</ref>}}
The Ho'Din people were tall, multi-color-skinned [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Moltok/Legends|Moltok]]. Ho'Din had long, suction cup-tipped fingers used for climbing [[Tree/Legends|trees]] and, on their heads, red-violet snake-like "hair" (fleshy tubes covered in scales) which acted as thermal sensors. They claimed to have evolved from [[Plant/Legends|plants]]&mdash;in fact, "Ho'Din" translated as "walking flower" in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]]. They were noted for possessing two hearts.

Their claims to botanical origins was probably a consequence of the nature-worshiping religion most Ho'Din followed, known as [[Dinante Fli'R]]. Most non-Ho'Din scientists found such claims unlikely, classifying them as reptilian instead. Whatever their origins, the Ho'Din were among [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] greatest [[Botanist/Legends|botanists]] and ecologists. [[Master Gardener]] was a title of respect among them.

==History==
In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], a [[Gender/Legends|female]] Ho'Din going by the name of [[Lohjoy]] served the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] as a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Engineer/Legends|engineer]].

Around [[300 BBY/Legends|300 BBY]], the tree-dwelling Ho'Din [[Plague on Moltok|gave up]] their low-technology lifestyle and moved to the forest floor. There, they began mining, farming, and manufacturing. However, their understanding of ecology was rudimentary, and they did not foresee the consequences of deforestation. The decaying organisms which formerly accelerated the decay of plant life on the forest floor became parasites which caused disease and malnourishment in their Ho'Din hosts. The Ho'Din were forced back to the trees, where they refocused their resources on ecological and botanical research.

The Ho'Din eventually developed herbal therapies which rid themselves of parasites. Their pharmacological techniques, combined with the eventual restoration of Moltok's ecosystem, allowed them to survive and prosper as a civilization. Other forms of technology were strictly regulated on Moltok, though off-world Ho'Din accepted them as a necessary evil when used on other, already "damaged", planets. Exports of Ho'Din plants and medicines made Moltok a very wealthy planet. Much of this wealth was spent in rejuvenating planets with damaged ecosystems, or creating "garden worlds" where all could commune with nature. Reverence for nature dominated Ho'Din society, with the [[Dinante Fli'R]] priests ruling Moltok.

==Ho'Din in the galaxy==
[[File:Iwo_Kulka.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Iwo Kulka]], just before his death at the hands of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]].]]
Most Ho'Din who lived away from Moltok were botanists. A few took advantage of their natural beauty and grace to become models or dancers. Many Ho'Din tended to be vain about their personal appearance.

In 32 BBY, a Ho'Din [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] of [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder/Legends|Gardulla the Hutt]] named [[Oo Wen]], conspired with a brave cadre of enslaved children from [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]&mdash;[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], [[Kitster Chanchani Banai|Kitster Banai]], the [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] [[Dorn (Bothan)|Dorn]], and the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Pala Kwi'teksa]]&mdash;to protect several [[Ghostling]] children from the Hutt in her new [[Gardulla's pleasure garden|pleasure garden]], the construction and maintenance of which Wen was charged with to oversee. After being introduced to the Ghostlings' peril, Wen, within the confines of his garden (which was itself, for the unwary, extremely perilous), secured safety for these delicate creatures of [[Datar/Legends|Datar]] until they could be smuggled off world.<ref name="EIA7">''[[Episode I Adventures 7: Capture Arawynne]]''</ref>

The healer and botanist [[Baji]] and the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Par'tah]] were Ho'Din. Two Ho'Din [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] survived the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and escaped [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]]&mdash;the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Iwo Kulka]] (who died later in the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]]), and [[Plett]], a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] who escaped to [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]].

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the Ho'Din were mostly left alone by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]. This was primarily due to the Ho'Din's aversion to technology and reverence for plant life, but may have also been influenced by the Ho'Din's similarity to the [[Shaper caste|Shapers]].

===Common Ho'Din names===
Common Ho'Din names included Kutu and Usta.<ref name="UAA">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref>
